Writing our system in matrix form, we get
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14155694/assets/2ddf89590d0999c5e4e4a0ff9fcd921ac5504b3ad1d32b9beef648d7fefe8db6.svg)
where ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14155694/assets/bd09972274cc36c682b0ea8995b0204a81ff1b534f035a71dc82e16feef5448b.svg) and ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14155694/assets/348604bfb51c09587767580ad1826c0265e68a209d9a32c3fc3a148aa585b327.svg) So, the matrix of the system is ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14155694/assets/eaa62ec8ac2c20ea9da57932ffb963385f053ddbb3635a733d61445653b7ff73.svg)

Given the system $\mathbf{x}'(t) = A \mathbf{x}(t)+\mathbf{g}(t),$ where $A$ is a constant square matrix, the solution of the initial value problem can be written as the sum of the homogeneous part and a particular solution:

$$
\mathbf{x}(t) = \underbrace{e^{A(t-t_0)} \, \mathbf{x}(t_0)}_{\text{homogeneous part}} + \underbrace{\int_{t_0}^{t} e^{A(t-s)} \mathbf{g}(s) \, \text{d}s}_{\text{particular solution}},
$$

where $\mathbf x(t_0)$ is the initial condition vector. 

Let's evaluate each part separately:

- First, we find the homogeneous part. We are given that 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14155694/assets/c4d8be4e05ff6f388a8de97537bd0b67ef2f8d1e3c740a0d4acbf1b3fa2806a0.svg)
Since the initial conditions are given at $t = t_0 = 0,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{A(t-{t}_{0})}x(0) & ={e}^{At}\,x(0) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{3t} & t{e}^{3t} \\ 0 & {e}^{3t}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

- Next, we find the particular solution. Notice that 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14155694/assets/636f82ca2fb40fbdaaff30937ec1309606023b11b161d6264982e34cddf501e5.svg)
So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{A(t-s)}g(s) & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{3(t-s)} & (t-s){e}^{3(t-s)} \\ 0 & {e}^{3(t-s)}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{3(t-s)} \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-3s+3t} \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{t}{e}^{A(t-s)}g(s)\,\text{d}s & ={\int }_{0}^{t}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-3s+3t} \\ 0\end{aligned}]\text{d}s \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{3}{e}^{-3s+3t} \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{s=0}^{s=t} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3}{e}^{3t}-\frac{1}{3} \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3}{e}^{3t}-\frac{1}{3} \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3}{e}^{3t}-\frac{1}{3} \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{3t}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14155694/assets/b9664098790934e75578bd236e43dc1da4588a085922c0cb81499e54cbd0e93c.svg)
